description: PER-FILE type-error baseline for libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator (mirrors packages/operator-core/.tsc-baseline.json and apps/operator-vite/.tsc-baseline.json, P-010/WI-4535/EI-847). A file whose current error count exceeds its baseline here is a NEW, ATTRIBUTED regression and gates lint:tsc:orchestrator (the gate NAMES the file).
note: 2026-08-02 (WI-6826): seeded from a fresh `tsc -p libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/tsconfig.json --noEmit --incremental false` snapshot, the FIRST time these 157 sources were ever typechecked (no tsconfig existed, so build:typecheck refused the package with project_not_found and lint:tsc covers only packages/operator-core). Every entry below is a TEST file: the 2 errors the run found in production source (readonly-array variance at both parseBlueprintLocalRoots call sites in src/invoke.ts) were FIXED in the same change rather than baselined, so orchestrator's src/ is at a strict ZERO and this file records test-fixture debt only. Do NOT read an entry as acceptable — read it as owed. The debt is stale fixtures that drifted while nothing typechecked them, in three verified shapes: (1) every `Expected 1 arguments, but got 2` (TS2554, 9 of the 59) is `expect(x).toBe(y, 'message')` — a Jest/Chai-style second MESSAGE argument that Vitest's toBe/toEqual do not accept. The assertion itself still asserts correctly, so these are NOT silent no-ops; what is silently discarded is the custom failure message, i.e. exactly the diagnostic that would explain WHY a byte-stability test failed. (2) TS2739 — the test's own makeInput() builds a BuildPromptInput missing genuinely-required fields (promptOverride/cwdOverride/featureId), so the fixture feeds `undefined` where production passes a string. (3) TS18048 — blueprint.spine.edges became optional and the assertions were never narrowed. Tracked separately from WI-6826.
